source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Lebanon campus is the largest published power figure in Ohio at 35 MW, but that ranking reflects disclosure habits, not the state's actual data center capacity.

The campus publishes 35 MW of IT capacity across two buildings inside 400,000 square feet of technical space. It does not publish rack count, power density, or tenants. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 35 MW is roughly 875 racks. At 10 kW per rack, typical of older enterprise halls, the same load is roughly 3,500 racks. The published number fixes the power, not the silicon.

The certification list, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and Green Globes, qualifies the campus for regulated workloads. None of it identifies who occupies the building.

Ohio has 79 mapped facilities, but only 9 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 118.4 MW. This campus is 35 MW of that, roughly 30 percent of the state's published capacity. That share measures what operators choose to disclose, not what has been built.
